sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Stuart McGill. 2012. The Kainji languages of Northwestern and Central Nigeria. Circulation draft, May 2012, 369 pp. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation.
sources.note: Sec. 3.6.4 'Gurmana' (p. 19): people/location only; 'Johnston (1919) includes a long wordlist of Gurmana... Stuart McGill has recorded a lengthy wordlist of Gurmana in 2012, and once this is analysed...'. Sec. 4.6.4 'Gurmana' under ch. 4 PHONOLOGY (p. 35) is an EMPTY heading. The string 'stress' occurs nowhere in the 369-page draft. Comparative wordlist has 'Gurmana-R' rows (Blench's own list, some tone marks) with no prosodic commentary.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2012 (ed. III) / 2020 (ed. IV). An Atlas of Nigerian Languages. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. Entry 'Gurmana' (no. 161 / 163).
sources.note: Entry: Niger State, Shiroro LGA, Gurmana town and nearby hamlets; >3,000 (1989); 'Source(s) Blench (1989)'. No grammar, phonology or wordlist reference given.

sources.citation: Johnston, Harry H. 1919. A Comparative Study of the Bantu and Semi-Bantu Languages, vol. I. Oxford: Clarendon Press.
sources.note: Gurmana = language no. 254; vocabulary (from Rev. W. P. Low, C.M.S., p. 815) appears as one column of the comparative tables (pp. ~732-746), entry p. 749. The only accent remark is the general orthographic note (pp. 40-41): 'The accent or pitch of the voice is indicated by \'. This is so normally and frequently on the penultimate syllable that the accent is only employed when an exception to the prevailing rule in Bantu transfers the voice-pitch to the first, last, or other syllable than the penultimate.' -- a blanket Bantu convention, not a statement about Gurmana.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken et al. 2021. Preliminary findings from a sociolinguistic survey of the Bauchi [bsf] - Fungwa [ula] language cluster of Niger State, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2021-062. SIL International.
sources.note: Mentions Gurmana [gvm] only as a neighbouring language and in the classification discussion; recommends future work on 'the linguistic relationships of Basa-Gurmana, Gurmana, and Pangu with Fungwa'. No Gurmana data.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2018. Nominal affixing in the Kainji languages of northwestern and central Nigeria. In John R. Watters (ed.), East Benue-Congo: Nouns, pronouns, and verbs, 59-106. Berlin: Language Science Press.
sources.note: Sec. 3.7 'The Shiroro languages', p. 94: 'MacDonell & Smith (2004) have circulated a phonology and grammar of Rin. For the other languages there is only wordlist data.' Table (p. 74): 'Gurmana -- Alternating affixes and concord'. Nothing on stress, accent or tone for Gurmana.

sources.citation: McGill, Stuart & Roger Blench. 2012. Documentation, development, and ideology in the northwestern Kainji languages. Language Documentation and Description 11: 90-135. doi:10.25894/LDD180
sources.note: Resource table, Shiroro branch (p. 100): '(Gurmana) -- Published wordlist (Johnston 1919), KJ700'. No descriptive work of any kind listed; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2011. The Shiroro languages (web page, rogerblench.info.../BC/Kainji/Shiroro/ShiOP.htm; Wayback capture 2015-04-20).
sources.note: One classification paragraph and a photo; no Gurmana document linked. Sibling lane's Wayback CDX of the whole Kainji folder shows no Gurmana wordlist or phonology file was ever posted.

sources.citation: Johnston, Harry H. 1922. A Comparative Study of the Bantu and Semi-Bantu Languages, vol. II. Oxford: Clarendon Press.
sources.note: Group H (S-B.) 'The Central Nigeria or Kaduna River languages' (pp. 182-183): Gurmana (254) prefixes and concords from G. A. J. Bieneman's 1920 vocabulary; phonology remark only that Group H 'makes more use of vowels'; nothing on stress or tone.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record gurm1246 (and Wikipedia 'Gurmana language', 'Shiroro languages').
sources.note: Glottolog lists no descriptive reference (only subclassification comments Blench n.d., McGill 2009/2012, and the Campbell et al. 2022 endangerment record); Wikipedia stubs cite only Ethnologue, Glottolog and Blench 2012.

sources.citation: McGill, Stuart. 2012. Gurmana wordlist (c. 700 items, KJ700 Kainji comparative database), unpublished field recording; noted in Blench & McGill 2012 sec. 3.6.4 and McGill & Blench 2012 p. 100.
